mismatch: A pointer-only cursor changes the initial base register and folds address arithmetic.
transformation: Keep an integer address temporary before assigning the typed pointer.

mismatch: Repeated constant call arguments are rematerialized rather than saved in high registers.
transformation: Try a register-qualified local for an existing initialized scalar.

mismatch: Postincrement pointer stores reorder memory operations and pointer updates.
transformation: Separate postincrement reads or stores from their cursor increment.

mismatch: The initial entry check and the loop continuation check need distinct placement.
transformation: Try an entry-guarded do/while preserving zero iterations.

mismatch: The stack base and scaled index appear in the opposite addition operand order.
transformation: Compute a byte offset first, then add the integer stack address and advance the pointer separately.

mismatch: The compiler keeps the loop offset and global sink in exchanged registers.
transformation: Name a word-global pointer before the loop; try its initializer alongside the other loop setup.

mismatch: A shared narrow result adds return shifts to a wide wraparound tail.
transformation: Return direct differences before the shared tail; test a full-width tail result.

mismatch: Equivalent offset subtraction chooses a different temporary and branch-sharing shape.
transformation: Distribute addition or subtraction around a grouped integer offset.

mismatch: A label-only outer loop keeps a frequently used mask in a high register.
transformation: Express the two-exit backedge as an infinite loop with explicit breaks.

mismatch: A tag loads into the scratch register and then copies into its saved register.
transformation: Test the masked tag directly instead of assigning it through the reused scratch variable.

mismatch: A reused arithmetic output reverses the addition operands.
transformation: Name the old output value before adding it to the saved base.

mismatch: The constant mask and saved tag arrive in the opposite low registers.
transformation: Assign the masked value as one expression instead of reusing the scratch variable for the mask.

mismatch: A redundant tag copy changes the later high-register copy into a low-register copy.
transformation: Test the saved tag directly rather than first assigning it to a reused scratch variable.
